gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mayan-nu: Contemporary through and through, Origami lays down a single-stroke brush line of constant width, with a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals can handle more size; its c gapes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-medefaid: Unique and contemporary, Origami cuts every stroke at a single engraver's depth, no deeper in places. Noto Sans Medefaidrin is the sans foil, its lowercase rising high and its curves free of ink pooling.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-meetei-m: No hairlines, just brush: Origami draws the whole alphabet at constant width, a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek, with its cracked-bangle rounds, can take a bigger size.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mende-ki: Noto Sans Mende Kikakui stands its lowercase tall against the capitals, with daylight through every curve. But Origami, a display face, draws with no thick-thin swell, unlike what a pointed brush would give.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mro: Zero stroke contrast defines Origami, a brush-lettered display face drawn at constant width. Noto Sans Mro sits opposite in sans-serif, dense and tall through the middle, with large entrances into each letter.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: One brush, one width: Origami is a monoline sign painter's hand. Noto Sans Myanmar lays a heavy-looking strip of text below, with a broad c, weighing against that single line.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-old-perm: Origami's lack of thick-thin swing makes it a pure single-stroke brush face, with a lowercase mass like poured lead. Noto Sans Old Permic gives it a friendly plain sans partner underneath.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: One thick thread: Origami feels traced in a single, unbroken line of brush. Noto Sans Osmanya, sans-serif with wide s turns and oversized lowercase, would carry paragraphs with ease.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Noto Sans PhagsPa has c openings you can see through and a gentle bump up from small letters to capitals. Origami's wire-like line quality is the standout, set against that sans-serif body.
